key_pathways: Hepatic esterase metabolism to active metabolite enalaprilat

avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone secretion, decreasing urinary potassium excretion and increasing serum potassium levels; additive hyperkalemic effect
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid potassium supplementation unless specifically prescribed by physician; monitor serum potassium levels regularly

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and antagonize ACE inhibitor efficacy; increase hyperkalemia risk and acute kidney injury
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, use lowest dose for shortest duration with renal function monitoring

avoid_supplements.name: Spironolactone and potassium-sparing diuretics
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both reduce potassium excretion; additive hyperkalemic effect with significant risk of cardiac arrhythmias
avoid_supplements.action: Use only with careful physician oversight and frequent potassium level monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: Licorice can cause sodium retention and potassium depletion, potentially counteracting ACE inhibitor benefits and affecting blood pressure control
caution_supplements.action: Limit licorice consumption; monitor blood pressure and electrolytes if use continues

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase blood pressure and potentially reduce antihypertensive efficacy of enalapril
caution_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor blood pressure response and adjust enalapril dose if needed

avoid_foods.name: High-potassium foods (excessive intake)
avoid_foods.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce renal potassium excretion; excessive dietary potassium intake increases hyperkalemia risk
avoid_foods.action: Moderate intake of potassium-rich foods (bananas, oranges, spinach, potatoes); discuss appropriate dietary potassium limits with healthcare provider

caution_foods.name: Salt substitutes (potassium chloride-based)
caution_foods.mechanism: Salt substitutes containing potassium increase serum potassium levels in presence of ACE inhibitor
caution_foods.action: Avoid or use regular salt as alternative; consult physician before using potassium-containing salt substitutes

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: May inhibit hepatic metabolism, though clinical significance is minimal with enalapril's renal clearance
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption acceptable; no strict avoidance required but monitor for increased effects

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium levels, renal function (creatinine, BUN, eGFR), and blood pressure regularly, especially when initiating therapy or adjusting doses. Educate patients on dietary potassium restriction and to report symptoms of hyperkalemia (weakness, palpitations, irregular heartbeat).
